articles.title: Stock market today: BSE Sensex jumps over 500 points, NSE Nifty50 above 24,550
articles.full_text: Benchmark indices open August on a firm note, extending the positive momentum seen in the previous session. BSE Sensex climbed 551.13 points, or 0.71 per cent, to trade at 78,645.77, while NSE Nifty 50 gained 168.45 points, or 0.69 per cent, to 24,552.05 in early trade. The upbeat start came as investors took comfort from easing crude oil prices and improving global sentiment after fresh diplomatic developments in the Middle East. Market participants also remained focused on the Reserve Bank of India's monetary policy meeting and the ongoing June-quarter earnings season, with several heavyweight companies set to announce their results. Foreign investor inflows, which turned positive in July after months of selling, also continued to support market sentiment. Indian benchmark indices might be headed for a steady start as crude prices continue to fall, tumbling almost 6% on Monday. Oil prices dropped sharply after US President Donald Trump said talks with Iran were expected to take place, raising hopes that tensions in West Asia could ease. In a post on Truth Social, Trump said Iran and other Middle Eastern countries had asked for more time to finalise a deal that would reopen the Strait and address concerns over Iran's nuclear programme. The possibility of easing tensions pushed Brent crude down by more than 6 per cent. Lower oil prices are usually good news for India, as the country imports most of its crude oil. Cheaper oil can help keep inflation under control and reduce import costs, improving the overall outlook for the economy. Brent crude later traded around $83.90 a barrel, while WTI crude was around $80.15, helping support positive sentiment in the stock market. Stock market today: Top stocks to buy this week ​Last week, benchmark indices staged a strong recovery, reversing their recent losing streak as multiple positive factors boosted investor confidence. BSE Sensex advanced 2,034.87 points, or 2.67 per cent, while NSE Nifty climbed 616.15 points, or 2.59 per cent. Analysts attributed the rally to easing crude oil prices, improving geopolitical sentiment, encouraging June-quarter corporate earnings and renewed buying by foreign institutional investors. The recovery reflected stronger risk appetite among investors after a period of market weakness. Positive domestic macroeconomic conditions also supported the gains, with participants expecting earnings momentum and policy developments to determine whether the upward trend could continue. Global developments continued to play a major role in shaping sentiment in stock market benchmarks. Investors closely tracked tensions in the Middle East, particularly the US-Iran conflict, as any further escalation could affect crude oil supplies through key shipping routes. Oil prices tumbled more than 6% on Monday as hopes of a diplomatic breakthrough between the United States and Iran erased part of last month's rally. However, uncertainty over the negotiations and persistent security risks along key shipping routes has kept investors on edge. As of 7:10 am, WTI crude was down 4.75% at $80.65 a barrel, while Brent crude fell 4.40% to $84.06 a barrel. Analysts said geopolitical developments were likely to influence global risk appetite and could trigger volatility across equity markets. While easing oil prices had supported market recovery in the previous week, traders remained cautious about fresh developments that could quickly alter investor sentiment and impact sectors sensitive to energy costs. Quarterly earnings remained one of the biggest stock-specific drivers for investors as several prominent companies prepared to announce their June-quarter financial performance. Market participants closely tracked results from companies including DLF, Bharti Airtel, ONGC, Hero MotoCorp, LIC and State Bank of India for insights into sectoral performance and the broader health of corporate India. Analysts noted that encouraging earnings from large companies had helped improve investor confidence in recent sessions. Strong earnings are expected to remain an important factor in determining stock-specific movements even as broader markets react to domestic policy decisions and global developments. Investors also looked for management commentary on demand trends, profitability and future business outlook. Foreign portfolio investors made a strong comeback to Indian equities after remaining net sellers for four consecutive months. During July, overseas investors infused Rs 20,200 crore into domestic equities, signalling an improvement in confidence towards Indian markets. Analysts attributed the renewed buying to attractive valuations after recent corrections, easing global headwinds and expectations of stronger corporate earnings. The return of foreign capital also coincided with improving market sentiment supported by healthy domestic macroeconomic indicators. Market participants continued to monitor whether the buying trend would sustain, especially with global uncertainties surrounding crude oil prices and geopolitical tensions. Continued foreign inflows are often viewed as an important support for benchmark indices and broader market sentiment. Dalal Street is entering a crucial session with several major events expected to influence investor sentiment over the coming sessions. The Reserve Bank of India's Monetary Policy Committee meeting emerged as the key domestic event, with market participants closely tracking any signals on interest rates and the central bank's economic outlook. Alongside the policy decision, the June-quarter earnings season continued to gather pace, with several large-cap and mid-cap companies scheduled to announce their financial results. Investors also remained alert to geopolitical developments in West Asia, particularly the US-Iran conflict, as any escalation could disrupt crude oil supplies and impact global financial markets. Besides these factors, manufacturing and services PMI data and foreign institutional investor activity were also expected to influence trading trends.

articles.description: The Consortium of National Law Universities will begin CLAT 2027 registrations today, August 3, at 10.00 am IST. Candidates can apply for undergraduate and postgraduate law programmes until October 31, while the entrance examination is scheduled for December 6. The examination pattern remains unchanged. Registration data from the past five years shows a consistent increase in applicants, with admissions available across 27 National Law Universities offering a limited number of seats.
